questions.question: How is the Cabin attribute handled during preprocessing in this experiment?

answers.a: It is encoded using One-Hot Encoding after preprocessing
answers.b: It is removed from the dataset due to missing values
answers.c: It is converted into a numerical attribute using Label Encoding
answers.d: It is normalized using feature scaling techniques

explanations.a: Cabin is treated as a categorical feature and is transformed into multiple binary columns using One-Hot Encoding.
explanations.b: The attribute is not removed; it is retained and processed.
explanations.c: Cabin is not label encoded; One-Hot Encoding is used instead.
explanations.d: Scaling is applied only to numerical features, not categorical ones.

questions.question: Suppose a numerical attribute contains several extreme outliers. Which imputation method would generally be more appropriate than mean imputation?

explanations.a: The median is less sensitive to extreme values and provides a more robust estimate for skewed distributions.
explanations.b: Mode is typically used for categorical variables rather than numerical attributes.
explanations.c: Label encoding converts categorical values to numbers and does not address missing values.
explanations.d: One-hot encoding is used for categorical features, not for filling missing numerical data.

questions.question: Why was the mode (most frequent value) used to fill missing values in the Embarked attribute?

answers.a: Because categorical variables cannot be averaged
answers.b: Because it increases the dataset size

explanations.a: Statistical measures such as mean or median cannot be applied directly to categorical variables.
explanations.b: Filling missing values does not change the number of records in the dataset.
explanations.c: Mode imputation replaces missing values but does not remove duplicates.
explanations.d: Dimensionality reduction is performed using other techniques such as PCA.

questions.question: Why must categorical variables such as Sex be encoded before applying machine learning algorithms?

answers.a: Because machine learning algorithms require numerical input
answers.d: Because encoding automatically improves model accuracy

explanations.a: Most algorithms perform mathematical operations and therefore require numerical representations of data.
explanations.b: Encoding does not reduce the number of records in a dataset.
explanations.c: Missing values must be handled separately before encoding.
explanations.d: Encoding enables model training but does not guarantee better accuracy.

questions.question: Which potential issue may arise when using One-Hot Encoding for categorical variables with many unique categories?

explanations.a: One-hot encoding creates a separate column for each category, which may lead to a large number of features.
explanations.b: One-hot encoding produces binary values (0 or 1), not negative numbers.
explanations.c: Encoding does not resolve missing value problems.
explanations.d: One-hot encoding increases feature dimensions rather than reducing them.

questions.question: Why is normalization applied to numerical features during preprocessing?

answers.a: To convert categorical variables into numerical form
answers.b: To bring numerical features to a comparable scale
answers.d: To reduce the number of features

explanations.a: Converting categorical variables into numbers is done using encoding.
explanations.b: Normalization ensures that features with larger numerical values do not dominate the learning process.
explanations.c: Missing values are handled using imputation techniques.
explanations.d: Normalization rescales feature values but does not remove features.

questions.question: Which type of machine learning algorithm is most sensitive to feature scaling?

answers.a: Distance-based algorithms such as K-Nearest Neighbors

explanations.a: These algorithms compute distances between data points, making them sensitive to feature magnitude differences.
explanations.b: Decision trees split data based on thresholds and are generally less affected by feature scaling.
explanations.c: Rule-based systems depend on logical conditions rather than feature scaling.
explanations.d: These systems are not machine learning algorithms.

questions.question: Which visualization technique is most suitable for identifying outliers in numerical data?

explanations.a: Histograms show the distribution of values but may not clearly highlight individual outliers.
explanations.b: Box plots explicitly show quartiles and whiskers, making outliers easy to detect.
explanations.c: Pie charts display proportions of categories rather than numerical distributions.
explanations.d: Bar charts are mainly used for categorical comparisons.

questions.question: Why is data visualization performed after preprocessing in this experiment?

answers.a: To verify whether preprocessing steps were applied correctly
answers.b: To automatically train a machine learning model

explanations.a: Visualization helps confirm successful normalization, encoding, and missing value handling.
explanations.b: Visualization helps in analysis but does not train models.
explanations.c: Visualization does not change the dataset size.
explanations.d: Duplicate removal is part of data cleaning, not visualization.

questions.question: After completing preprocessing and feature engineering, what is the next logical step in a machine learning workflow?

explanations.a: Once the dataset is cleaned and structured, it becomes suitable for model development.
explanations.c: Labeling generally happens earlier in the pipeline.
explanations.d: Feature removal is a preprocessing decision rather than the next pipeline stage.
